definition: Positive self-talk is a person’s spontaneous inner speech with a positive tone, such as thoughts they direct toward themselves in sport or competition. In the source, it is linked with greater self-confidence and better performance when it occurs in the competitive situation.

reasons: The definition adds unsupported framing by describing the term as “inner speech” and as thoughts people “direct toward themselves”; the packet only supports spontaneous self-talk in sport, not those specific characterizations.

The performance/self-confidence relationship is misstated: the source says positive self-talk in sport predicted self-confidence, which then predicted positive situational self-talk in competition, and that positive situational self-talk predicted performance. It does not support the claim that the term itself is linked with greater self-confidence and better performance when it occurs in the competitive situation.
The packet does not explicitly define “positive self-talk” as “inner speech with a positive tone”; it only describes “positive and negative spontaneous self-talk” in the context of sports.

The packet supports links between positivity and self-confidence and between positive situational self-talk in competition and performance, but the definition’s phrasing “when it occurs in the competitive situation” is not directly supported as a single combined claim tying positive self-talk (as defined in the first sentence) to improved performance in that exact way.
